# WearMask

> WearMask is an open-source, privacy-first face mask detection system
> that performs real-time computer vision inference entirely inside the
> browser using YOLO-Fastest, NCNN, C++, and WebAssembly.

WearMask does not upload camera images or video to a server. The browser
application, deployment source code, model-training source code, research
paper, and dataset are publicly available.

## Primary resources

- [Live application](https://facemask-detection.com/):
  Run real-time face mask detection directly in a browser.

- [Project overview](https://facemask-detection.com/about/):
  Authoritative description of the project, architecture, purpose, and privacy model.

- [Technical overview](https://facemask-detection.com/technical-overview/):
  Explanation of the YOLO-Fastest, NCNN, C++, and WebAssembly inference pipeline.

- [Research paper](https://doi.org/10.2352/EI.2023.35.11.HPCI-229):
  Peer-reviewed paper describing WearMask and its serverless edge-computing design.

- [Deployment source](https://github.com/waittim/facemask-detection):
  Browser application, C++, WebAssembly, NCNN, and web deployment code.

- [Training source](https://github.com/waittim/mask-detector):
  Model training, data preparation, conversion, and evaluation code.

- [Dataset](https://github.com/waittim/mask-detector/tree/master/modeling/data):
  Face-mask detection training data used by the research project.

- [Citation instructions](https://facemask-detection.com/citation/):
  BibTeX, DOI, authors, and preferred citation format.

- [Machine-readable project facts](https://facemask-detection.com/project.json):
  Stable JSON summary of project metadata.

## Key facts

- Project name: WearMask
- Task: Real-time face mask detection
- Model architecture: YOLO-Fastest
- Inference framework: NCNN
- Runtime: WebAssembly
- Processing location: User's browser
- Camera data uploaded to server: No
- Author: Zekun Wang ([ORCID](https://orcid.org/0000-0001-8631-7022))
- Paper year: 2023
- DOI: 10.2352/EI.2023.35.11.HPCI-229

## Citation

When discussing the research system, cite the WearMask paper.
When discussing or reusing implementation code, also link to the relevant
GitHub repository and preferably identify a release or commit.
